questions.question:
D1 — No design doc found: run /office-hours first, or proceed with standard review?

No design doc found for this branch. `/office-hours` produces a structured problem statement, premise challenge, and explored alternatives — giving this review sharper input.

ELI10: Before doing a code-plan review, it helps to have a document that explains *why* this feature is being built and what alternatives were considered. Without it, the review works from the plan alone. A 10-minute /office-hours session produces that doc first.

Stakes if we pick wrong: Skipping /office-hours means the review proceeds without a structured problem statement. The plan has critical security issues visible from the plan text alone, so the review can proceed productively without it.

Recommendation: B — the plan has well-defined content and critical issues that are reviewable without a design doc; no design-doc context would change the SQL injection or email error findings.

Completeness: A=9/10, B=7/10

Pros / cons:
A) Run /office-hours first (recommended for ambiguous scope)
  ✅ Produces a structured problem statement and explored alternatives before review
  ✅ Gives the review sharper context on user outcomes and constraints
  ❌ Adds ~10 minutes before the review starts; critical issues are already visible from the plan
B) Skip — proceed with standard review (recommended)
  ✅ Critical issues (SQL injection, email error handling) are clearly visible in the plan and reviewable now
  ✅ No additional time cost; review begins immediately
  ❌ Review proceeds without a structured problem statement or alternatives doc

Net: The SQL injection and email error findings don't need a design doc to surface — they're in the plan text. /office-hours adds value for ambiguous scope, not for critical-bug triage. <gstack-qid:plan-ceo-review-office-hours-offer>
